documents.title: Adaptive Gradient Clipping for Noisy Small-Batch Optimization
documents.abstract: A controlled study compares adaptive clipping with fixed clipping in noisy small-batch optimization.
body: Adaptive Gradient Clipping for Noisy Small-Batch Optimization

Methods. We ran 120 matched training trials with batch size eight and injected label noise. The adaptive threshold used a moving percentile of recent gradient norms. Fixed clipping and no clipping were preregistered comparison conditions.

Results. Adaptive gradient clipping reduced divergent runs from 18 percent to 4 percent. Median validation accuracy among converged runs changed by less than one percentage point. The result therefore supports improved stability, not a general accuracy gain.
Limitations. The experiment covered one convolutional architecture, batch sizes from eight to sixteen, and synthetic label noise. We did not test large-batch training or transformer pretraining.
documents.expected_evidence: Adaptive gradient clipping reduced divergent runs from 18 percent to 4 percent.

documents.title: Boundary Conditions for Adaptive Clipping under Momentum
documents.abstract: A replication examines adaptive clipping when high momentum and correlated gradient noise are present.
body: Boundary Conditions for Adaptive Clipping under Momentum
Methods. We repeated the small-batch protocol with momentum 0.95 and temporally correlated gradient noise across 80 matched trials.

Results. Divergence was 11 percent with adaptive clipping and 10 percent with fixed clipping, a difference that was not statistically distinguishable. Adaptive clipping also required 7 percent more optimization steps to reach the target loss.

Interpretation. These results contradict a universal stability benefit. They do not refute the earlier result under independent noise; instead they identify momentum and correlated noise as boundary conditions.
documents.expected_evidence: Divergence was 11 percent with adaptive clipping and 10 percent with fixed clipping, a difference that was not statistically distinguishable.

body: Adaptive Signal Clipping in Marine Acoustic Sensors
This report concerns acoustic hardware saturation. It does not study gradients, optimization, machine learning training, or batch size.
